chunks: And from him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zurārah, from ʿĪsā ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Hāshimī, from his father, from his grandfather, from ʿAlī عليه السلام, who said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “Indeed, the pillar of the religion is salat (prayer), and it is the first thing from the deeds of the son of Adam that is looked into. So if it is sound, his deeds are considered; and if it is not sound, the rest of his deeds are not considered.”

key_terms.ابْنِ آدَمَ: the human being, literally the son of Adam
key_terms.الدِّينِ: the religion, meaning the structure of religious life and commitment
key_terms.عَمُودَ: the supporting pillar or central support

ai.seo_question: Why is salat (prayer) described as the pillar of religion and the first deed examined?
ai.summary: This hadith presents salat (prayer) as the central pillar of the religion and the foremost deed examined from a person's actions. Its soundness determines whether the rest of one's deeds receive consideration, showing its foundational place in worship and reckoning.
